summary: Added an opt-in return_request_metrics field to OpenAI-compatible chat and completion requests. Measured queue, first-token, generation, end-to-end, mean inter-token, and output-throughput values are returned under sglext.request_metrics without enabling global metrics. Default response shapes are unchanged, streaming emits one terminal extension chunk, and unavailable or undefined values are omitted instead of serialized as zero.

tests.what_was_measured: Baseline reproduction: the checked-out request schema silently discarded the requested opt-in field. Raw output: /job/reproduction-before.txt

Nine timing tests, including exact derived latency/throughput values, omission for undefined single-token interval metrics, and per-request timing transport without global metrics. Raw output: /job/test-req-time-stats.txt

Twenty-two completion serving tests covering opt-in isolation, serialization without zero placeholders, internal propagation, and final streaming sglext placement before [DONE]. Raw output: /job/test-serving-completions.txt
One hundred thirty-six chat serving tests, including distinct per-choice request metrics and existing response/streaming compatibility. Raw output: /job/test-serving-chat.txt

One assigned AMD Instinct MI355X executed a 4096-element numerical check against an independent CPU result; max absolute error was 1.1920928955078125e-07 and allclose passed. This verifies the prepared Torch/ROCm GPU environment, not the HTTP feature itself. Raw output: /job/gpu-check.txt

remaining_limitations: No end-to-end model server was launched because the prepared environment did not provide a local model checkout or weight path; request schema, timing propagation/calculation, response construction, serialization, multi-choice isolation, and streaming ordering were validated directly.

GPU evidence is limited to the prepared-environment numerical check recorded in /job/gpu-check.txt: one AMD Instinct MI355X, max_abs_error 1.1920928955078125e-07 versus CPU, allclose true. It is not evidence for the HTTP response-path behavior.
The embedded Rust server is outside the requested scope.
No native C++ or FlyDSL source changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
